page.layout: One page of text in a single column, headed by a Hebrew running head. The entries are a Hebrew lexicon with Latin glosses, printed as paragraphs with Hebrew words in bold. No margin notes.

main_text.p: נָהַג Duxit, (Rexit, Gubernavit) Abduxit, Abegit; Adduxit, Deduxit, Induxit. Præter. אותי נהג Me ducit, Thr.3.2. נֶהֶגוּ Abduxerunt, 2.Sam.6.20[?]. Part. נֹהֵג Ducens, Ductor, Dux, Psal.80.2. Plur. נְהָגִים Ducentes erant, Ducebant, 1.Sam.6.3. Pih. Præter. נִהַגְתָּ עַמְּךָ Duxisti populum tuum, Jesa.63.14. &c.
מִנְהָג m. Ductus: ומנהג כמנהג יהוא Et ductus sicut ductus Jehu est, 2.Reg.9.20. ubi & constructum. Apud Rabbinos etiam est Ritus, Consuetudo.
נָהַד Lamentatus est, Lamentum edidit. Præt. ונהה נהי Et lamentabitur lamentum, Mich.2.v.4. Imper. נְהֵה Ede lamentum, Ezech.32.18. Niph. Futur. וַיִּנָּהוּ Et lamentati sunt, 1.Sam.7.2.
נָהָה m. Idem, Ezech.7.11. est q; forma שָׁדַד à שָׁדַד. Nam ה affumit pronunciationis causâ Mappik.
נִי m. Idem; Ezech.27.32. & est ficut רוה à רי: Aff. בְּנֵיהֶם In lamento suo; Ezech.27.32.

נָהַל Pih. Duxit, Deduxit, commodè & leniter: Præt. נִהַלְתָּ Commodè ducis, Exod.15.13. Partic. אֵין מְנַהֵל לָהּ Non erat ductor ei, Jesa.51.18. Futur. יְנַהֵל Leniter ducet, Jesa.40.11. וַיְנַהֲלֵם Et duxit eos, Gen.47.17. Hithp. Futur. אֶתְנַהְלָה Ducem præbebo me, vel, leniter incedam, Genes.33.14.

נָהַם Rugiit: Fremuit, Gemuit: Leonum proprie. Præt. וּנְהַמְתָּ Gemasq; in novissimo tuo; Prov.5.11. וּנְהַמְתֶּם Et gemetis, Ezech.24.23. Particip. אֲרִי נֹהֵם Leo rugiens, Prov.28.15. Futur. וַיִּנְהַם Et fremet, Jes.5.29.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points are approximated where the scan is blurred; the consonants are as far as they can be read. Doubtful: the page number (459 or 450), the reference "2.Sam.6.20" (possibly 36.20 or 6.20), the form of the root heading in the third entry (נהר or נהד), and the Hebrew in the entry for מנהג and in the Ezekiel 7.11 entry. The gloss "Lamentabile vel Lamentitum" is set as printed. The bottom Hebrew word at the lower right is treated as a catchword.
